title: compact attention core: token-aware scheduler + shadow-kv prefetch to reduce tail latency
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: customer workloads with highly skewed request sizes (short chat messages interleaved with long context generations) were exposing p95/p99 latency spikes despite aggressive batching. Investigation showed two contributing factors: (1) the scheduler was coalescing tokens without awareness of prefix-hotness leading to oversized batches that pushed some requests into longer KV read paths, and (2) KV cache cold-misses for recently-used key ranges created stalls while the decoder waited on memory transfer.

This PR introduces two complementary runtime improvements to reduce tail latency and improve throughput: (A) a token-aware continuous batching scheduler (CompactScheduler) that maintains small fast-path batches for low-token requests while opportunistically coalescing larger requests, and (B) a shadow-KV prefetcher that tracks recent token window footprints and proactively stages KV shards into GPU-local memory for predicted next-chunk accesses. Together these reduce p95 by ~28% and p99 by ~41% on mixed chat/long-gen workloads in our internal canary.

What changed (high level):
- runtime/scheduling/compact_scheduler.{cc,h}: new scheduler implementing a token-aware policy with exponential backoff thresholds and a quick-path queue for <=8-token requests.
- runtime/kv/shadow_prefetch.{cc,h}: new lightweight prefetcher that observes KV index access traces and issues low-priority memcpy streams to warm caches. Prefetch policy is adaptive and throttles based on GPU memory pressure.
- runtime/attn/kernel_glue.cc: small refactor to expose a prefetch hook and a compact-batch fast path in the attention dispatch.
- runtime/attn/compact_attention.cu: new compact attention kernel optimized for small batch sizes and short sequences; uses fused rotary application inline with q/k computation to avoid extra memops. Kernel is mixed-precision friendly and contains guards for nvcc compute capability fallbacks.
- tests/perf/bench_compact_scheduler.py and bench/fixtures: new benchmarks and dataset to reproduce mixed short/long patterns.
- docs/perf/compact-scheduler.md: operational notes and recommended config knobs for Dedicated pools.

Checklist: 
- [x] Scheduler algorithm implemented with unit tests
- [x] Kernel integrated and smoke-tested on Ampere+ and Hopper GPUs
- [x] Prefetcher respects mem pressure and does not OOM in stress tests
- [x] Microbenchmarks and end-to-end canary run included

Benchmarks (canary, perf lab, NVIDIA A100, single-GPU):
- Mixed chat (80% <=8 tokens, 20% long gens): p50: 6.2ms (baseline 6.5ms), p95: 24.1ms (baseline 33.6ms), p99: 46.3ms (baseline 78.5ms)
- Long-only (seq_len=1024): throughput up 7% (tokens/sec) compared to baseline fused-attn path due to better kernel selection heuristics.
- GPU utilization: average utilization stable; memory copy overlap increased by ~12% due to low-priority prefetch streams.

Compatibility and safety:
- Prefetcher is opt-in via runtime config (redwood.runtime.shadow_prefetch = true) and off by default for Private deployments.
- CompactScheduler is behind a rollout flag; default behavior unchanged for existing clusters.
- No public API changes.

Follow-ups:
- Integrate with SmartRouting to use tenant-level workload profiles to further tune thresholds (ENG-4870).
- Explore combining shadow prefetcher with KV shard placement metadata to pre-stage only colocated shards.

References: Linear ENG-4721 (attn tail latency), bench/issue-312 memory-overlap investigation.
